title: BioinfoIPBLN/reanatax pipeline parameters
description: Taxonomic profiling of the non-host fraction of public or local sequencing data - fetch, QC, host depletion with HISAT2, and Kraken2/Bracken classification.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to a comma-separated samplesheet describing the input FASTQ files.
input.help_text: Three columns with a header row: `sample`, `fastq_1` and `fastq_2` (leave `fastq_2` empty for single-end data). Rows that share a `sample` value are treated as multiple runs of that sample and are concatenated. Mutually exclusive with `--input_dir` and `--input_accessions`.

input_dir.description: Path to a folder of already-downloaded FASTQ files.
input_dir.help_text: Files are discovered with `--fastq_pattern` and mates are paired from their file names (`_1`/`_2`, `_R1`/`_R2`, `_R1_001`/`_R2_001`, with `.` or `_` as separator). Use `--single_end` to disable mate detection. Mutually exclusive with `--input` and `--input_accessions`.

input_accessions.description: One or more ENA/SRA accessions to download with fastq-dl, comma-separated or as a file with one per line.
input_accessions.help_text: BioProject (PRJEB/PRJNA/PRJDB), Study (ERP/DRP/SRP), BioSample (SAMD/SAME/SAMN), Sample (ERS/DRS/SRS), Experiment (ERX/DRX/SRX) and Run (ERR/DRR/SRR) accessions are supported. Each accession is first resolved to its list of runs so that every run downloads as its own parallel task. GEO accessions (GSE/GSM) are not supported by fastq-dl - use the linked SRA study instead. Mutually exclusive with `--input` and `--input_dir`.

fastq_pattern.description: Glob used to find FASTQ files under `--input_dir`.
fastq_pattern.help_text: Note the leading `**.` rather than `**/*.`: in Nextflow globs, `**/` requires at least one directory level, so `**/*.fastq.gz` would silently skip files sitting directly in `--input_dir`.

single_end.description: Treat every file found under `--input_dir` as a separate single-end sample.
single_end.help_text: Escape hatch for folders where mate detection would misfire, e.g. sample names that legitimately end in `_1`.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

download_options.title: Download options
download_options.description: Control how raw reads are fetched when `--input_accessions` is used.

fastqdl_provider.help_text: ENA is the default because its FASTQs are served directly, whereas SRA downloads have to be converted and recompressed. fastq-dl falls back to the other archive when an accession is missing entirely, but NOT when an archive lists a file it cannot then serve - use `--fastqdl_sra_runs` for that.

fastqdl_sra_runs.description: Comma-separated run accessions to fetch from SRA regardless of `--fastqdl_provider`.
fastqdl_sra_runs.help_text: For runs whose ENA copy is broken: the index and FTP listing report the file, but every fetch fails. Naming the run here changes only that task's command, so the rest of the cohort keeps its cache entries.

group_runs_by.description: How runs are grouped into samples before analysis.
group_runs_by.help_text: `experiment` (the default) concatenates the technical replicates of one library into a single sample, which is what most submissions intend. `run` keeps every run separate. `sample` merges everything sequenced from the same BioSample.

max_download_forks.description: Maximum number of downloads running at the same time.
max_download_forks.help_text: Raising this speeds up large BioProjects but archives throttle (and eventually refuse) aggressive clients, so increase it gradually.

download_local.description: Run the download tasks on the local executor even under `-profile slurm`.
download_local.help_text: Useful on clusters whose compute nodes have no outbound internet access.

save_download_metadata.description: Publish the archive metadata tables that describe each downloaded run.

reference_genome_options.title: Host reference options
reference_genome_options.description: The host genome that reads are aligned against before classification.
reference_genome_options.help_text: Give exactly one of `--hisat2_index`, `--fasta`, `--host_accession` or `--host_taxid`. They are listed here in order of decreasing precedence: a prebuilt index short-circuits everything else, and a local FASTA is used in preference to downloading one.

host.description: Host reference(s): NCBI accession, taxid, genome FASTA or prebuilt HISAT2 index. Comma-separated for two.
host.help_text: One parameter for every way of naming a host reference; what each entry is is detected from the value. `GCF_*`/`GCA_*` is an assembly accession, digits alone are a taxonomy ID, a directory (or `.tar.gz`) is a prebuilt HISAT2 index, and anything else on disk is a genome FASTA. Up to four references are depleted against in the order given - a read must fail against every one of them to be called non-host - and the first is the primary one that `--gtf`, Qualimap and `--quantify_host` describe. Example: `--host GCF_000001405.40,/data/chm13.fa`.

fasta.description: Path to the host genome FASTA file (optionally gzipped). Superseded by --host.
fasta.help_text: Accepts a comma-separated list, and may be combined with the other host-reference options. Up to four references are supported and reads are depleted against them in turn: a read must fail against every one of them to be called non-host. The classic pairing is GRCh38 plus T2T-CHM13, which catches the centromeric, satellite and structurally variant reads missing from GRCh38 that would otherwise be classified as microbes. Further entries are for sequence the library genuinely contains but the primary assembly does not - a blood meal, a graft, a co-cultured cell line - or for a synthetic reference such as UniVec or PhiX. The FIRST reference given is the primary one: --gtf describes it, and it is the one Qualimap reports on and --quantify_host counts against.

gtf.description: Optional host annotation GTF, used to build a splice-aware HISAT2 index.
gtf.help_text: Only worth providing for RNA-seq input, where splice-aware alignment captures more host reads. Building the index then needs roughly `--hisat2_build_memory` of RAM.

hisat2_index.description: Path to a prebuilt HISAT2 index directory, or a `.tar.gz` of one. Superseded by --host.
hisat2_index.help_text: Accepts a comma-separated list, and may be combined with the other host-reference options. Up to four references are supported and reads are depleted against them in turn: a read must fail against every one of them to be called non-host. The classic pairing is GRCh38 plus T2T-CHM13, which catches the centromeric, satellite and structurally variant reads missing from GRCh38 that would otherwise be classified as microbes. Further entries are for sequence the library genuinely contains but the primary assembly does not - a blood meal, a graft, a co-cultured cell line - or for a synthetic reference such as UniVec or PhiX. The FIRST reference given is the primary one: --gtf describes it, and it is the one Qualimap reports on and --quantify_host counts against.

host_accession.description: NCBI assembly accession of the host genome to download, e.g. `GCF_000001405.40`. Superseded by --host.
host_accession.help_text: Accepts a comma-separated list, and may be combined with the other host-reference options. Up to four references are supported and reads are depleted against them in turn: a read must fail against every one of them to be called non-host. The classic pairing is GRCh38 plus T2T-CHM13, which catches the centromeric, satellite and structurally variant reads missing from GRCh38 that would otherwise be classified as microbes. Further entries are for sequence the library genuinely contains but the primary assembly does not - a blood meal, a graft, a co-cultured cell line - or for a synthetic reference such as UniVec or PhiX. The FIRST reference given is the primary one: --gtf describes it, and it is the one Qualimap reports on and --quantify_host counts against. `GCF_` accessions are fetched from RefSeq and `GCA_` accessions from GenBank; the pipeline picks the right section for you. Set `--ncbi_group` to the organism's group (e.g. `vertebrate_mammalian`) to make the lookup much faster.

host_taxid.description: NCBI taxonomy ID of the host, e.g. `9606` for human. Superseded by --host.
host_taxid.help_text: Accepts a comma-separated list, and may be combined with the other host-reference options. Up to four references are supported and reads are depleted against them in turn: a read must fail against every one of them to be called non-host. The classic pairing is GRCh38 plus T2T-CHM13, which catches the centromeric, satellite and structurally variant reads missing from GRCh38 that would otherwise be classified as microbes. Further entries are for sequence the library genuinely contains but the primary assembly does not - a blood meal, a graft, a co-cultured cell line - or for a synthetic reference such as UniVec or PhiX. The FIRST reference given is the primary one: --gtf describes it, and it is the one Qualimap reports on and --quantify_host counts against. Resolves to that taxon's RefSeq reference assembly. Use `--host_accession` when you need a specific assembly version.

ncbi_group.help_text: `all` always works but downloads every group's assembly summary first. Narrowing it (`vertebrate_mammalian`, `bacteria`, `fungi`, `plant`, `viral`, ...) is considerably faster.

hisat2_build_memory.description: Memory required before hisat2-build will use splice sites and exons.
hisat2_build_memory.help_text: Building a splice-aware index for a vertebrate genome needs roughly 200 GB of RAM; below this threshold the module silently builds the (much cheaper) genome-only index instead.

save_reference.description: Publish the downloaded genome and the HISAT2 index so later runs can reuse them.

univec.description: Deplete against UniVec (vector, adapter, linker and primer sequence) as a final pass
univec.help_text: Its own pass rather than another --host entry, because a vector database needs different alignment stringency: --very-sensitive expands to `--score-min L,0,-1`, which lets a 100 bp read carry roughly 25 mismatches and still align. Against a genome that catches diverged host sequence; against a 3 kb plasmid backbone it deletes real reads. So this pass does not inherit --hisat2_args. CAVEAT: UniVec's plasmid and phage backbones contain genuine E. coli and coliphage sequence, so on a study where those organisms are the question this removes signal rather than noise. Runs last, and also works with --skip_host_removal.

univec_source.description: The vector database to deplete against
univec_source.help_text: Defaults to NCBI's UniVec_Core, the reduced-redundancy subset. Point it at UniVec itself for the full set, or at a local FASTA to run offline.

univec_hisat2_args.description: HISAT2 arguments for the UniVec pass; replaces --hisat2_args entirely

univec_save_bam.description: Keep the vector alignments as a sorted BAM

adapter_fasta.description: FASTA of adapter sequences to pass to fastp.
adapter_fasta.help_text: Only needed when fastp's automatic adapter detection is not enough.

save_trimmed_fail.description: Publish the reads that fastp discarded.

remove_rrna.description: Remove ribosomal RNA with SortMeRNA before host depletion.
remove_rrna.help_text: For total-RNA/RiboZero libraries, where rRNA is typically 94-99% of the reads. Runs between trimming and host depletion, so HISAT2 and everything after it see a library that is already rRNA-free and the read-accounting denominators stay correct. Pointless on poly(A)-selected or DNA libraries. Requires `--sortmerna_db`.

sortmerna_db.description: rRNA reference FASTA(s) for SortMeRNA, comma-separated.
sortmerna_db.help_text: The SortMeRNA distribution ships these as a separate `database.tar.gz` download (Silva 138 SSURef NR99 + RFAM 14.1), e.g. `smr_v4.3_sensitive_db.fasta`. Multiple files may be given, comma-separated. Required when `--remove_rrna` is set.

sortmerna_index.description: Prebuilt SortMeRNA index directory. Built once per run if omitted.
sortmerna_index.help_text: SortMeRNA 6.0 replaced CMPH with BBHash in the index format, so an index built by 4.x cannot be read by 6.x/7.x. Point this at an index built with the same version the pipeline runs, or leave it unset and let the run build its own.

sortmerna_args.help_text: `--index 0`, `--paired_in` and `--out2` are set by the pipeline and should not be repeated here.

host_depletion_options.title: Host depletion options
host_depletion_options.description: HISAT2 alignment against the host genome.

hisat2_args.help_text: `--very-sensitive` expands to `--bowtie2-dp 2 -k 50 --score-min L,0,-1`. The `-k 50` part reports up to 50 alignments per read, which makes the host BAM large and the run slower; see `--hisat2_max_alignments`.

hisat2_chunk_size.description: Align this many read pairs per task instead of the whole library at once (0 disables).
hisat2_chunk_size.help_text:
HISAT2's memory grows with how much a single process has aligned, and only a fresh process resets it; with `--very-sensitive` on libraries of a few hundred million pairs it has been observed in the hundreds of GB. Chunking runs one HISAT2 process per slice, so the ceiling is set by the chunk rather than by the library.

The slices are offsets, not files. HISAT2's `-s/--skip` and `-u/--upto` count reads-or-pairs, so each chunk task opens the same FASTQ and aligns its own window - nothing is split, recompressed or written to scratch. The chunks are independent tasks, so they also run in parallel, which is usually the larger win: the longest step in the pipeline becomes as many short tasks as the executor will schedule.

The per-chunk BAM, summary and non-host FASTQs are joined back into exactly the files an unchunked run produces, so nothing downstream behaves differently. 5000000 is a reasonable starting point. See also `--hisat2_chunk_memory`.

hisat2_chunk_memory.description: Memory requested per chunk task when --hisat2_chunk_size is set.
hisat2_chunk_memory.help_text: The peak a chunk reaches scales with `--hisat2_chunk_size`, which the pipeline cannot infer, so it is a knob rather than a formula. The default suits chunks of a few million pairs; raise it alongside the chunk size.

hisat2_max_alignments.description: Report at most this many alignments per read (hisat2 `-k`).
hisat2_max_alignments.help_text: Set to `1` to keep the search sensitivity of `--very-sensitive` while writing only the best alignment. Recommended whenever the host BAM is only used for QC or for counting host reads.

save_host_bam.description: Sort, index and publish the host-aligned BAM files.

save_unaligned.description: Publish the non-host (unaligned) FASTQ files that are fed to Kraken2.

qualimap_gff.description: Optional GFF/GTF passed to Qualimap BamQC for feature-level statistics.
qualimap_gff.help_text: Deliberately separate from --gtf (which only controls the splice-aware HISAT2 index): a full vertebrate annotation makes BamQC dramatically slower, so this is opt-in rather than inherited.

quantify_host.description: Count host reads per gene with featureCounts. Requires --gtf.
quantify_host.help_text: Turns the host half of the split from a QC by-product into an expression matrix, measured from the same library as the microbial profile - which is what makes host/microbiome correlation defensible, since both sides share the same technical batch. The BAM needs no preparation: the HISAT2 module already pipes through `samtools view -F 256`, so each read appears once. Counts come from the first host reference given.

featurecounts_feature_type.description: GTF feature type to count over (featureCounts -t).

featurecounts_attribute.description: GTF attribute to group features by (featureCounts -g).

require_both_mates_unmapped.description: Release a read pair as non-host only when NEITHER mate aligned. On by default.
require_both_mates_unmapped.help_text: With this off, the non-host FASTQs are HISAT2's `--un-conc-gz` output: every pair that failed to align CONCORDANTLY, so a pair with one unambiguously host mate leaves whole and is then classified as host. On, a variant module drops `--no-mixed --no-discordant` and splits the alignment stream on explicit SAM flags - `-F 4 -F 8` for the host BAM, `-f 12` for the non-host FASTQ. Measured across four vulvar-swab RNA libraries this took host carry-over from 0.5-13.5% to 0.0% at a flat cost of 2.7-3.6% of non-host reads. Those costs are not equivalent: the loss is uniform across samples and leaves composition unchanged, while carry-over is sample-specific and biases comparisons between samples. It is also slower, because HISAT2 now looks for discordant and single-mate alignments it previously skipped.

kraken2_db.description: Path to a Kraken2 database directory, or a `.tar.gz` of one.
kraken2_db.help_text: Prebuilt databases are available from https://benlangmead.github.io/aws-indexes/k2. The directory must contain `hash.k2d`, `opts.k2d` and `taxo.k2d`, plus `databaseNmers.kmer_distrib` files if Bracken is to run.

kraken2_confidence.help_text: Raising this (0.05-0.2 is typical) trades sensitivity for far fewer spurious classifications, which matters most for low-biomass samples.

kraken2_min_hit_groups.description: Minimum number of hit groups needed to make a classification call.

kraken2_memory_mapping.description: Read the database from disk instead of loading it into RAM.
kraken2_memory_mapping.help_text: Drastically lowers the memory request at the cost of speed. On a machine where the database already sits in the page cache (for example a fast shared filesystem with plenty of free RAM) this is often close to free, and it is what makes many-sample runs against a large database practical.

kraken2_use_daemon.description: Classify via `k2 classify --use-daemon`, keeping the database resident between samples.
kraken2_use_daemon.help_text: The legacy `kraken2` wrapper reloads the whole index on every invocation - about 30 minutes per sample for a 340 GB database on network storage. The daemon loads it once into a background process that outlives the task. Tasks run one at a time (the daemon's control FIFO is not concurrency-safe), which costs nothing once the index is resident. The daemon is addressed through hardcoded paths in /tmp, so it is shared with anything else using k2 on that node, and it KEEPS HOLDING THE INDEX after the run finishes: stop it with `k2 clean --stop-daemon`. Incompatible with a tarballed `--kraken2_db` and with `--kraken2_memory_mapping`.

kraken2_daemon_timeout.description: Upper bound on one `k2 classify --use-daemon` call, as a `timeout` duration.
kraken2_daemon_timeout.help_text: The daemon is reached through FIFOs in /tmp, and nothing in that handshake has a deadline: a client that opens them when no daemon is listening blocks in open(2) indefinitely, at 0% CPU and with an empty log, and because the daemon tasks run one at a time the rest of the cohort queues behind it. The local executor does not enforce `time`, so this is what actually bounds the wait. On timeout the task fails with a signal status and is retried, and the retry clears the stale /tmp state so a fresh daemon is started. The default covers a cold index load of a ~340 GB database plus a large library; raise it if single libraries take longer than that to classify.

kraken2_report_minimizer_data.description: Add per-clade distinct-minimizer columns to the Kraken2 report.
kraken2_report_minimizer_data.help_text: Useful for filtering false positives, but the extra columns cannot be read by Bracken or by MultiQC, so this requires `--skip_bracken`.

kraken2_save_reads.description: Publish the classified and unclassified FASTQ files produced by Kraken2.

kraken2_save_readclassifications.help_text: One line per read - these files are large.

kraken2_memory.help_text: Must be at least the size of the database unless `--kraken2_memory_mapping` is used. Defaults to 72 GB (16 GB with memory mapping), which suits Standard-8/PlusPF but not core_nt.

run_metaphlan.description: Also profile the non-host reads with MetaPhlAn.
run_metaphlan.help_text: MetaPhlAn maps against clade-specific marker genes rather than classifying every read by k-mer, so it reports relative abundance over a curated set and is far more conservative than Kraken2. Additive: `--run_metaphlan --skip_kraken2` uses it instead of Kraken2, while leaving Kraken2 on runs both over the same reads - which is the only way to see where the two disagree on one library. Requires `--metaphlan_db` and `--metaphlan_index`.

metaphlan_db.description: Directory holding the MetaPhlAn bowtie2 index and its .pkl.

metaphlan_index.description: MetaPhlAn index basename inside --metaphlan_db, e.g. mpa_vJan25_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202503.

metaphlan_args.help_text: `-t rel_ab_w_read_stats` adds the estimated_number_of_reads_from_the_clade column, which count-based differential-abundance methods require. Do not set --input_type, --db_dir, --index, --nproc, --tmp_dir, --mapout or -o; the module sets those.

run_sylph.description: Also profile the non-host reads with sylph.
run_sylph.help_text: sylph calls a species from the containment ANI of its reference genome against the reads (reported when >= 95%), instead of classifying reads one by one, which makes far fewer false positives than per-read classification. Additive: `--run_sylph --skip_kraken2` uses it instead of Kraken2, and adding `--skip_host_removal` skips alignment as well, since a host genome that is not in the database cannot be called. It assigns no reads, so a sylph-only run carries every restriction of `--skip_kraken2`. Its documented floor is 0.01-0.05x coverage of a bacterial genome, and it assumes the reads sample the whole genome: on RNA-seq, and 3' single-cell libraries above all, a present organism can fall under 95%, so a missing call is weak evidence of absence.

sylph_db.description: One or more sylph databases (.syldb or .syl2db), comma-separated.
sylph_db.help_text: Pre-built databases (GTDB, IMG/VR, RefSeq fungi, ...) are listed at https://sylph-docs.github.io/. The pipeline runs sylph 1.0.0, so the two-stage .syl2db format works. Reads are sketched at sylph's default c = 200; for a database sketched at another c, pass it in `--sylph_args` (e.g. `-c 100`), because reads and database must match. Genomes below ~10 kb, HIV-1 among them, need a -c 100 database: sylph wants more than 50 sketched k-mers to report a genome.

sylph_taxonomy.description: sylph-tax taxonomy metadata file(s) for the --sylph_db databases, comma-separated. Optional.
sylph_taxonomy.help_text: sylph reports genome files, not taxa; these tables map each genome file to a lineage and have to be the ones built for the databases profiled against. Pass files, not sylph-tax's built-in identifiers such as GTDB_r232: those resolve through a folder under $HOME that a container does not have. A custom table is two columns - genome file name, then a semicolon-delimited lineage (d__...;p__...;...;s__...). Without it, only sylph's genome-level output is written. The pre-built tables carry GTDB taxonomy, whose names and species boundaries differ from the NCBI taxonomy Kraken2 reports.

sylph_args.help_text: For example `-c 100` for a -c 100 database, `-u` to estimate the unknown fraction and report true rather than effective coverage, or `--min-number-kmers` for genomes too small for the default. Do not set -t, -o, -r, -1 or -2; the module sets those.

sylph_tax_args.help_text: For example `--annotate-virus-hosts` with a pre-built viral database. Do not set -t; the module passes --sylph_taxonomy there.

run_metax.description: Also profile the non-host reads with Metax.
run_metax.help_text: Metax aligns reads to a genome collection and keeps a taxon only if its reads cover the genome the way random sampling would (observed over expected breadth, OEBR), which drops artifacts from contaminated references, kitome fragments and shared conserved regions. It reports NCBI taxids. Additive: `--run_metax --skip_kraken2` uses it instead of Kraken2. No public container exists - see --metax_container. Its authors note that coverage-based filtering can drop true taxa in RNA-derived data, so on transcriptomes a missing call is weak evidence of absence.

metax_db.description: A Metax database: its metax_db.json, or the directory holding it.
metax_db.help_text: Pre-built cross-domain databases from NCBI RefSeq (2025: 33,533 genomes; 2022: 33,143) are linked from https://github.com/hzi-bifo/Metax. The whole directory is used, because maCMD finds the index files through the JSON. Build a custom one with `metax index`.

metax_dmp_dir.description: NCBI taxonomy dump for Metax (nodes.dmp, names.dmp, merged.dmp, delnodes.dmp).
metax_dmp_dir.help_text: Unpack https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/taxonomy/taxdump.tar.gz. A GTDB or ICTV dump works too, if the database was built with its taxids.

metax_args.help_text: For example `--mode recall` (identity 0.95, aligned fraction 0.60) or `--mode precision`, `--min-cbreadth`, or `--host` for pathogen mode. Do not set --db, --dmp-dir, -i, -p, -o or -t; the module sets those.

metax_save_readclassifications.help_text: One line per read with the most likely taxid and the likelihood of every candidate. Off by default because it is a line per read; Metax does not write it at all for a fractional index.

metax_container.description: A container image providing metax and maCMD.
metax_container.help_text: Metax is published on its author's conda channel (zldeng), not on bioconda, so no public image exists. Without this, `-profile wave` builds one from the module's conda environment, `-profile conda` or `mamba` installs it, and otherwise METAX_PROFILE needs metax and maCMD on the host PATH.

bracken_db.description: Path to the Bracken kmer distributions. Defaults to `--kraken2_db`.

bracken_read_length.description: Read length for Bracken (-r), or 'auto' to measure it.
bracken_read_length.help_text: Bracken's -r must match a k-mer distribution the database was built with, not merely your reads: a mismatch does not fail, it silently returns wrong abundances. 'auto' takes the mean read length after trimming from fastp, per sample, and snaps it to the nearest `database<N>mers.kmer_distrib` present in the database, warning if the gap is large. Give a number to pin it.

bracken_level.description: Taxonomic level for Bracken abundance re-estimation.

bracken_threshold.description: Minimum number of reads at the chosen level before Bracken re-estimates it.

min_rel_abundance.description: Relative abundance a taxon must exceed to be kept in the combined tables.
min_rel_abundance.help_text: Applied with --min_samples to the combined tables only; per-sample reports are left intact. This is a sparsity filter, NOT a contamination caller: with no negative controls it cannot tell a reagent contaminant from a rare real organism, it only removes taxa too sparse for any statistic to speak about. Without it the long tail of single-read hits dominates every distance metric. Dropped taxa are written to a `.removed.tsv` next to the filtered table.

min_samples.description: Number of samples in which --min_rel_abundance must be exceeded.

drop_host_taxon.description: Remove the host taxon from the combined tables and renormalise.
drop_host_taxon.help_text: Reads the depletion step missed are still classified, and while the host row sits in the table every microbial abundance is a fraction of host + microbes rather than of microbes. This drops the rows for `--host_carryover_taxid` and rescales the fraction columns against what is left. Exact for the Bracken table, which is flat; for the hierarchical Kraken2 combined report only the host's own rows go, and its ancestors keep their original clade counts. Dropped rows are written to the `.removed.tsv`, and the unfiltered combined table is published either way.

drop_host_clade.description: Also drop every taxon under the host's own clade at this rank.
drop_host_clade.help_text: Host leakage does not stop at the host taxid: a host read that misses the host genome is assigned to the nearest relative the database holds. Measured on the CSI-Microbes 10x cohort with Homo sapiens already dropped, Pan/Pongo/Gorilla/Macaca/Tupaia were still 84% of everything called microbial in the uninfected library -- 0.1% at genus, 58-66% at family, 71-88% at class. The lineage is read from the run's own Kraken2 reports. This is a prediction from the taxonomy, not a measurement of the reads, so leakage landing outside the clade (conserved or low-complexity matches to unrelated genomes) is untouched -- that is what --host_kmer_filter is for. High ranks are destructive by design: class on a xenograft deletes the mouse.

exploremetatax_bundle.description: Write a tar.gz of the taxonomic tables for the exploreMetaTax Shiny app.
exploremetatax_bundle.help_text: Produces `exploremetatax/reanatax.exploreMetaTax.tar.gz`. The app (https://shiny-public.fgcz.uzh.ch/app/exploreMetaTax) has no archive upload: extract the tarball, tick 'Browse a folder' on its Upload tab, pick the extracted folder and choose the input format. The bundle is a flat directory whose filenames are rewritten to match the app's per-format filters - a plain tar of `--outdir` would skip the Bracken tables entirely and load two other files under the wrong format. Includes whichever of Kraken2, Bracken, MetaPhlAn and HUMAnN actually ran, plus `--da_metadata` if given.

krakenuniq_db.description: KrakenUniq database directory. Setting it enables the KrakenUniq route.
krakenuniq_db.help_text: KrakenUniq cannot read a Kraken2 index, so this is a separate database you supply (build it with `krakenuniq-build`, or fetch a prebuilt one). The route is additive: it runs alongside Kraken2 unless you also pass `--skip_kraken2`. Its report adds per-taxon distinct-k-mer counts (`kmers`, `dup`) and reference coverage (`cov`), estimated by HyperLogLog - the discriminator Kraken2 approximates with distinct minimizers, at roughly five times the resolution. Bracken is not run on this route: Bracken's k-mer distributions belong to a Kraken2 database.

krakenuniq_args.description: Extra arguments for the KrakenUniq database preload.
krakenuniq_args.help_text: Passed to the single `krakenuniq --preload` that runs before the batch. Setting `--preload-size` here switches the module out of whole-database preloading, which is how you classify against a database larger than the node's memory.

krakenuniq_classify_args.description: Extra arguments for each KrakenUniq classification.

krakenuniq_save_reads.description: Keep the classified/unclassified FASTQs from KrakenUniq.

minimizer_filter.description: Drop taxa whose reads cover no breadth of their reference.
minimizer_filter.help_text: An abundance threshold asks how many reads landed on a taxon - the question a spurious call passes, since reads piled on one conserved locus look abundant. This asks how much of the reference they actually cover, using Kraken2's distinct-minimizer columns (needs `--kraken2_report_minimizer_data`) or KrakenUniq's `kmers`/`dup`/`cov`, which its reports carry already. Taxa below `--minimizer_min_reads` are never judged: too few reads to show breadth either way. Writes an evidence table so every decision is auditable, and the removals go through the same filter step, and the same `.removed.tsv`, as the abundance filter.

minimizer_min_reads.description: Only judge taxa holding at least this many reads.

minimizer_min_distinct.description: A taxon must cover at least this many distinct minimizers/k-mers.

minimizer_max_duplication.description: ...and its observed/distinct ratio must stay below this.
minimizer_max_duplication.help_text: The average number of times each distinct minimizer was re-hit. A real organism spreads reads over its genome, so most of what it hits is new; a call from one locus re-hits the same handful repeatedly.

minimizer_min_coverage.description: ...and cover this fraction of its reference. 0 disables the test.
minimizer_min_coverage.help_text: KrakenUniq reports coverage directly. For Kraken2 the denominator is read from `inspect.txt` in the database directory, whose second column is the distinct minimizers held per clade; the test is skipped if that file is absent. Coverage is confounded with sequencing depth - a genuinely rare organism also covers little - so it is off by default.

min_reads.description: Absolute per-taxon read floor, applied together with --min_rel_abundance.
min_reads.help_text: The relative threshold is computed against the MICROBIAL total, and after host depletion that total is small - Salzberg's TCGA reanalysis left a median of 2.6M non-host reads, 0.48% of the library - so 0.1% of it can be three reads on one conserved locus. Gihawi et al. (mBio 2023) filter to genus counts >=10; PRISM will not attempt confirmation below 10 reads and calls its score reliable only above ~100. Applied as AND with the relative threshold, on the count columns even when the table also carries fractions. 0 disables, which is the previous behaviour.

minimizer_distinct_scale.description: Scale the distinct-minimizer threshold with library depth. 0 disables.
minimizer_distinct_scale.help_text: Effective threshold = max(--minimizer_min_distinct, scale x classified reads). Sun et al.'s F1-optimised threshold sweep found the optimal unique-k-mer cut is linearly associated with sequencing depth (p = 7e-7) at about 0.002 unique k-mers per read, refining KrakenUniq's original 'about 2000 unique k-mers per million reads'. A flat threshold across libraries differing 100-fold in depth - normal in public-data reanalysis - is wrong in both directions at once. The same work found the distinct-k-mer axis is the single best Kraken-family filter (highest F1 in all three regimes tested) and that the read-count axis is unnecessary once it is applied, and that Kraken2 MINIMIZERS need a threshold 2-3x higher than KrakenUniq k-mers for equal F1. Suggested starting point: 0.002, or 0.005 to include the Kraken2 correction.

minimizer_correlation.description: Also require a taxon's reads, k-mers and distinct k-mers to rise together across samples.
minimizer_correlation.help_text: SAHMI's sample-level denoising (Ghaddar, Blaser & De, Nat Comput Sci 2023). The thresholds above ask whether a taxon's evidence is broad enough; this asks whether it scales. All three Spearman correlations - reads~k-mers, reads~distinct, k-mers~distinct - must be significant after BH correction, at genus or species rank, for a taxon seen in at least three samples. Catches what the thresholds cannot: a contaminant sitting at a flat low level in every library has plenty of distinct minimizers but its counts do not track. Needs at least 5 samples - with n samples the smallest attainable two-sided Spearman p is 2/n!, so at n=4 nothing can reach 0.05 and the run is refused rather than dropping everything.

minimizer_correlation_p.description: BH-adjusted p-value each of the three correlations must clear.

host_kmer_filter.description: Drop taxa whose reads mostly carry host k-mers, whatever they were classified as.
host_kmer_filter.help_text: SAHMI's per-read host test, applied to bulk data. Alignment-based depletion is not exhaustive, and what it misses is a genuine read with genuine k-mers - invisible to any filter that judges a taxon by its counts. Kraken2's read-level output records which taxon each run of k-mers was assigned to, so a read carrying host k-mers is recognisable even when the read as a whole was called a bacterium. Requires --kraken2_save_readclassifications, and requires the host to be present in the Kraken2 database: core_nt contains Anopheles gambiae, PlusPF does not. The run fails rather than reporting a clean result if no host k-mer is seen at all.

host_kmer_taxid.description: Taxid(s) counted as host by --host_kmer_filter. Defaults to --host_carryover_taxid.
host_kmer_taxid.help_text: Comma-separated. The host species alone by default; adding its genus or family catches k-mers Kraken2 could only place higher up, at the cost of condemning their genuine relatives too.

host_kmer_max_fraction.description: Drop a taxon once this fraction of its reads carry host k-mers.

host_kmer_min_reads.description: Taxa below this many reads are left to the abundance filter instead.

decontam.description: Identify reagent contaminants with decontam, using negative controls.
decontam.help_text: The only filter here given an external measurement of the kit, and so the only one that can separate a reagent contaminant from a genuinely rare organism - every other filter judges a taxon by its own evidence and is blind to that distinction. Opt-in because most public datasets carry neither blanks nor DNA concentrations. Scored on the combined Bracken table (flat species-level counts; a combined kreport is a hierarchy and would count the same reads at every rank), so it cannot be combined with --skip_bracken. The taxids it calls go to the abundance filter alongside the other evidence filters.

decontam_metadata.description: Sample metadata TSV for decontam. Falls back to --da_metadata.
decontam_metadata.help_text: First column is the sample id as the pipeline names it; remaining columns are factors. The negative controls have to have been run through the pipeline like any other sample, so they appear as columns in the combined table.

decontam_neg_value.description: Value in that column which marks a negative control. Compared case-insensitively.

decontam_conc_column.description: Metadata column holding post-PCR DNA concentration, for the frequency method.
decontam_conc_column.help_text: The frequency method needs no blanks. It tests whether a taxon's relative abundance falls as total DNA rises, which is the signature of a constant amount of contaminating template diluted by varying amounts of real sample. Values must be positive numbers.

decontam_method.help_text: `prevalence` needs --decontam_neg_column; `frequency` needs --decontam_conc_column; the other three need both. `either` calls a contaminant if either test does, `minimum` takes the smaller p-value, `combined` fuses them into one statistic.

decontam_threshold.description: decontam score below which a taxon is called a contaminant.

decontam_batch_column.description: Metadata column grouping samples into batches for decontam
decontam_batch_column.help_text: Contamination is a property of the kit, not of the study. Pooled across two sequencing runs or two extraction days, a taxon heavy in one batch and absent from the other looks like a real organism that varies between samples. Naming the column that separates the runs scores each batch against its own negative controls and combines the verdicts. Every batch must contain at least one control and two true samples, or the run fails rather than returning an unscored batch.

decontam_batch_combine.description: How per-batch decontam verdicts are combined
decontam_batch_combine.help_text: Only used with --decontam_batch_column. 'minimum' (decontam's default) takes the smallest p across batches, so a taxon condemned in any one batch is condemned overall - the right stance when a contaminant was only present in one run. 'product' and 'fisher' require agreement across batches and are more conservative. The per-batch calls are written to the evidence table either way.

shuffle_control.description: Classify a shuffled copy of every library as a negative control
shuffle_control.help_text: Runs Kraken2 a second time over the same reads with each read shuffled, so that its length, GC content and dinucleotide frequencies survive and none of its k-mers do. Whatever the database still reports is what it produces from base composition alone - the one number none of the other filters can supply, since they all judge a taxon's evidence on its own terms with no measurement of what that evidence is worth against noise. Taxa whose shuffled count reaches --shuffle_max_ratio of their real count are added to the drop list. Costs one extra Kraken2 pass; with --kraken2_use_daemon the database is already resident and that pass is close to free.

shuffle_method.help_text: 'dinuc' is an Altschul-Erickson Euler-path shuffle preserving the exact dinucleotide frequency as well as the base composition, and is the default because most compositional bias is dinucleotide-level. 'mono' permutes the bases and preserves GC content only, so it is a weaker null. 'reverse' reads each sequence backwards - not reverse-complemented, which would still map - preserving every compositional statistic including the trinucleotide spectrum, at the cost of leaving palindromic and low-complexity stretches intact.

shuffle_seed.help_text: Fixed rather than optional: a control whose result changes between runs of the same pipeline is not a control.

shuffle_reads.description: Shuffle only the first N fragments per sample (0 = all)
shuffle_reads.help_text: Subsampling makes the control cheap but raises its detection floor: one chance read in a subsample stands for several in the full library, so no taxon below scale/--shuffle_max_ratio real reads can be flagged. That floor is computed and printed, and taxa under it are reported as untested rather than clean.

shuffle_max_ratio.description: Flag a taxon once shuffled/real reads reaches this ratio

shuffle_min_reads.description: Below this many real reads a taxon is left untested

pathseq_microbe_bwa_image.description: Microbe BWA index image for GATK PathSeq; enables the PathSeq route
pathseq_microbe_bwa_image.help_text: PathSeq is the only classifier here that is not k-mer based: it ALIGNS the surviving reads to a microbe reference with BWA and divides an ambiguously mapping read between the taxa it hits, rather than pushing it up to their common ancestor. So it can place at species level what Kraken2 can only place at a genus, and it is not fooled by the composition-driven chance matches --shuffle_control measures. Additive with Kraken2; combine with --skip_kraken2 to use it alone. Needs Broad's prebuilt resource bundle - this pipeline does not build the index images, which are large, slow and specific to a reference choice.

pathseq_microbe_dict.description: Sequence dictionary (.dict) for the PathSeq microbe reference

pathseq_host_bwa_image.description: Optional host BWA image for PathSeq's own host filter
pathseq_host_bwa_image.help_text: Give this together with --pathseq_host_kmers, or neither. Skipping PathSeq's host filter is reasonable here because HISAT2 has already done that job and the reads reaching PathSeq are the ones it could not place; supplying both runs it as a second, alignment-plus-k-mer pass over what was left behind.

pathseq_host_kmers.description: Host k-mer file that goes with --pathseq_host_bwa_image

pathseq_save_bam.help_text: It holds every read PathSeq aligned tagged with its call, and is the size of the library. Only worth keeping when the individual alignments will be looked at.

pathseq_rank.description: PathSeq `type` kept in the combined tables
pathseq_rank.help_text: PathSeq's `type` column spells the rank out (species, genus, family, ...) rather than using a Kraken rank code. Leave unset to keep every row.

run_prism.description: Run PRISM to confirm candidate taxa against independent evidence
run_prism.help_text: PRISM (sjdlabgroup/PRISM) is not a classifier: it takes candidate taxa and tries to CONFIRM each one with full-length BLAST against nt, the GenBank annotation those alignments land on, host mapping with STAR and minimap2, and k-mer composition at every rank, then scores it with an XGBoost model over forty features. It runs on the TRIMMED reads, not the non-host ones, because it does its own host removal and several of its features are statistics of that removal. Not packaged anywhere - see --prism_path.

prism_path.help_text: The clone alone is not enough. It must also hold `genbank/` (the processed GenBank RDS files, distributed separately by the authors) and `sorted_accession_map.txt` (built once with blastdbcmd against the BLAST database). The run fails at validation if this is missing.

prism_container.description: Container image for PRISM; required under docker/singularity
prism_container.help_text: PRISM is an R script that shells out to Kraken2, minimap2, STAR, BLAST and SeqKit, and no public image carries that set, so there is no default. Build one from modules/local/prism/run/environment.yml, or use -profile conda which builds that environment directly.

prism_kraken_db.description: Kraken2 database for PRISM; defaults to --kraken2_db

prism_blast_db.description: BLAST nt database for PRISM's confirmation pass

prism_star_genome_dir.description: Host STAR index, for PRISM's own host depletion

prism_minimap2_index.description: Host minimap2 index, for PRISM's own host depletion

prism_min_read_per.description: PRISM's minimum reads per X to analyse

prism_barcode_only.description: Read 1 is barcode+UMI: drop it before PRISM sees the library
prism_barcode_only.help_text: Required with --single_cell. On 10x chemistry read 1 carries no biological sequence, so without this PRISM classifies and BLASTs it as cDNA. This is stricter than PRISM's own --barcode_only flag, which reaches only its BLAST step while its Kraken2 pass still runs --paired over both mates; here the barcode read is discarded before PRISM starts, so every step works on the cDNA read alone. For PRISM's literal behaviour, leave this false and pass --prism_args '--barcode_only TRUE'.

prism_score_threshold.description: Median PRISM score below which a taxon is called a contaminant
prism_score_threshold.help_text: Aggregated as the median across the samples that saw the taxon - not the mean, which one confidently-scored library drags either way, and not 'any sample', which on a large cohort condemns everything.

prism_min_reads.description: Below this many reads in every sample, leave the taxon untested

prism_filter.description: Apply PRISM's verdict to the combined Bracken table as a second filter pass
prism_filter.help_text: Off by default: PRISM scores the whole trimmed library while Bracken profiles the non-host fraction, so the two agree on taxids but were asked about slightly different read sets. Read the evidence table before letting it remove anything.

gene_diversity_filter.description: Flag taxa whose reads pile onto one locus instead of spreading over the genome
gene_diversity_filter.help_text: PRISM's argument, answered from HUMAnN's species-stratified gene-family table, so it needs --run_humann and no new reference. Every other filter counts reads or the k-mers behind them; none can see WHERE those reads landed, and a thousand reads on one conserved gene passes all of them. With --humann_regroup set it runs a second time on the regrouped table, which is the difference between many gene families and many PRODUCTS - a taxon can reach dozens of UniRef90 families that all encode the same thing.

gene_diversity_min_families.description: Distinct gene families a taxon must reach

gene_diversity_max_top_fraction.description: ...with no single family carrying more than this share of its abundance

gene_diversity_min_abundance.description: Below this pooled abundance a taxon is left untested

run_sparcc.description: Infer a taxon co-occurrence network with SparCC (FastSpar)
run_sparcc.help_text: An ordinary correlation matrix on compositional data manufactures negative associations everywhere, because the counts sum to a library size with no biological meaning; SparCC works on log-ratio variances, which are invariant to it. The run is refused outright when the cohort is too small for the bootstrap p-values to reach the Benjamini-Hochberg threshold for the number of pairs tested - an empty network from such a run means 'this cohort cannot be asked', not 'there are no associations'. --sparcc_force overrides.

sparcc_min_prevalence.description: A taxon must be seen in this fraction of samples

sparcc_min_reads.description: ...with at least this many reads there

sparcc_iterations.description: SparCC iterations for the point estimate

sparcc_permutations.help_text: Sets the p-value floor at 1/permutations. With many pairs that floor can sit above what Benjamini-Hochberg requires, in which case no edge could be called significant however strong its correlation - the run is refused with the number of replicates it would need.

sparcc_min_correlation.description: |rho| an edge needs before it is reported

sparcc_p_threshold.description: Adjusted p threshold for an edge, across every pair at once

sparcc_force.description: Run SparCC even when the cohort cannot support it

run_diversity.description: Alpha diversity, and how much of the between-sample variation each metadata variable explains.
run_diversity.help_text: Follows Llorens-Rico et al. (Nat Commun 2021): counts are CLR-transformed and compared by Euclidean distance (the Aitchison distance, which respects the fact that sequencing yields compositions), each metadata variable is tested on its own with a distance-based RDA for an adjusted R-squared and a permutation p-value, and a stepwise model then reports the variation each adds that the others do not - the gap between the two IS the confounding. PERMANOVA is reported alongside. Runs on the FILTERED combined Bracken table, unlike differential abundance, because diversity indices apply no filter of their own and observed richness on an unfiltered table is largely a count of database artefacts. Metadata is optional: without it you still get alpha diversity and an ordination.

diversity_metadata.description: Sample metadata TSV for the variance partitioning. Falls back to --da_metadata.

diversity_permutations.description: Permutations for the dbRDA and PERMANOVA tests.

trim_low_complexity.help_text: Homopolymer and near-homopolymer reads - poly-A tails, poly-G from two-colour chemistry - classify to whatever genome happens to hold that run, which is how a low-complexity artefact becomes a confident species call. SAHMI applies the same idea at its own quantitation step. Off by default because it removes reads, and a read removed at trimming is invisible to every count downstream. Appended to --fastp_args rather than replacing it.

low_complexity_threshold.description: fastp complexity threshold, as a percentage of bases differing from the next.

single_cell.description: Single-cell route: barcode-aware host alignment with STARsolo, and a cell-by-taxon matrix.
single_cell.help_text: REPLACES HISAT2 host depletion rather than supplementing it. In bulk, host depletion discards the host reads; in single cell they are the other half of the experiment (the cell-by-gene matrix) and the cell barcode is the only thing joining them to the microbial reads, so one barcode-aware aligner has to do both jobs in one pass. The non-host reads come out as an ordinary single-end FASTQ with the corrected barcode folded into each read name, so Kraken2, Bracken, Krona, the evidence filters and the exploreMetaTax bundle all run on them unchanged - the pseudobulk profile and the cell-by-taxon matrix come from the same classification and cannot disagree. fastq_1 must be the barcode+UMI read and fastq_2 the cDNA read. Requires --gtf and --kraken2_save_readclassifications.

star_index.description: Prebuilt STAR index directory or tarball for the single-cell route.
star_index.help_text: It must have been built with an annotation: STARsolo assigns reads to genes at alignment time, so a --sjdbGTFfile supplied later cannot rescue a matrix from an index built without one.

sc_chemistry.help_text: 10xv2 = CB 16 / UMI 10; 10xv3 and 10xv4 = CB 16 / UMI 12. `custom` requires --sc_cb_len, --sc_umi_start and --sc_umi_len. Getting the geometry wrong produces a run that completes with almost every barcode unmatched, which is easy to miss.

sc_whitelist.description: Cell barcode whitelist, or 'None' to accept every observed barcode uncorrected.
sc_whitelist.help_text: The whitelists ship with Cell Ranger, not with STAR, so this has to be supplied: 737K-august-2016.txt for 10xv2, 3M-february-2018.txt for 10xv3, 3M-3pgex-may-2023.txt for 10xv4. Passing 'None' disables correction, which lets a single sequencing error in a barcode manufacture a new cell.

sc_cell_filter.description: STARsolo --soloCellFilter, which separates cells from empty droplets.

sc_star_args.description: Extra arguments appended to the STARsolo command.

sc_min_frac.description: Share of a read's k-mers that must fall inside the assigned taxon's lineage.
sc_min_frac.help_text: SAHMI's min_frac. Guards against a read scattered across the tree being credited in full to whichever tip won the LCA.

sc_max_homopolymer.description: Drop reads with a single-nucleotide run longer than this. 0 disables.
sc_max_homopolymer.help_text: SAHMI's nFilter, whose default of 130 is very permissive - on a 150 bp read it only catches sequences that are ~87% homopolymer. Reading the FASTQ is only done when this is non-zero, since the sequences are not in Kraken2's output.

sc_ranks.description: Ranks to tabulate the cell-by-taxon matrix at, comma-separated codes.

sc_host_taxid.description: Taxid(s) whose k-mers disqualify a read. Falls back to --host_kmer_taxid, then --host_carryover_taxid.

sc_kmer_denoise.description: Require a taxon's total and distinct k-mers to rise together across cells.
sc_kmer_denoise.help_text: SAHMI's barcode-level denoising, and the same question --minimizer_correlation asks across samples, at a much finer grain: a library has thousands of barcodes but a study has few samples, so this has real power where the sample-level test needs at least five libraries. A barcode carrying more of a real organism carries proportionally more DISTINCT k-mers too; ambient contamination smeared over every droplet, or reads piling on one conserved locus, saturates. The distinct k-mers are recovered from the reads themselves - Kraken2's per-read output run-length encodes which taxon each consecutive k-mer matched, so the k-mers assigned to a taxon can be pulled out of the sequence. A taxon whose distinct count never moves while its read count does fails outright, since Spearman is undefined there but the meaning is not.

sc_kmer_len.description: Kraken2's k. 35 for the standard databases.

sc_min_barcodes.description: A taxon must be seen on at least this many barcodes to be tested (SAHMI uses >3).

sc_correlation_p.description: BH-adjusted p the barcode-level correlation must clear.

sc_max_barcodes_per_taxon.description: Cap on barcodes held per taxon (SAHMI's nsample). 0 removes the cap.
sc_max_barcodes_per_taxon.help_text: Bounds memory: without it an abundant taxon in a deep library holds a distinct-k-mer set for every droplet.

sc_min_umis.description: UMIs a taxon needs in a cell to be called present there.
sc_min_umis.help_text: CSI-Microbes' presence rule (Robinson et al., Sci Adv 2024). It is a hard threshold, not a test: on their positive control, requiring >=2 UMIs removed 100% of contaminant genera at single-cell level, which is a stronger result than any correlation-based filter here achieves. The authors call the cutoff arbitrary themselves (their stated limitation 2), so a sensitivity sweep over 1-5 is always written alongside the matrix and no conclusion should rest on one value. Calibrated for 10x 3'v3/5' with a strict cell filter; not validated for 3'v2 or plate data.

sc_adjust.description: Multiple-testing correction for the barcode-level correlation.
sc_adjust.help_text: SAHMI calls R's p.adjust() without naming a method, so it gets R's default - holm, controlling family-wise error rate rather than FDR. Kept as the default here to match.

sc_cell_metadata.description: TSV of barcode, sample, cell_type [, host_umis]. Enables cell-type enrichment.
sc_cell_metadata.help_text: Cell types are the one input this pipeline cannot produce - STARsolo gives a count matrix, not clusters - so bring them from Seurat/scanpy. A `sample` column is MANDATORY: enrichment is computed within each sample and combined afterwards, because pooling cells across samples with different cell-type compositions can inverting the result entirely (Simpson's paradox; CSI-Microbes devotes a methods paragraph and a counterexample to it). `host_umis` is optional but enables the doublet check that any co-occurrence claim needs.

sc_apply_drop_list.description: Apply the evidence filters' drop lists to the cell-by-taxon matrix, not only to the cohort tables.
sc_apply_drop_list.help_text: The minimizer filter, shuffled-read control, decontam and host k-mer scan all produce drop lists. Without this they reach only the combined Kraken2 and Bracken tables, so the enrichment test keeps testing taxa the pipeline has already judged false - and pays the multiple-testing cost for every one of them. Turn it off to inspect the unfiltered matrix.

sc_cooccurrence_min_cells.description: A taxon must infect this many cells to enter the co-occurrence test.

sc_enrichment_p.description: BH-adjusted p for calling a cell type enriched.

sc_umi_dedup.description: Count distinct UMIs per cell and taxon rather than reads.
sc_umi_dedup.help_text: On by default. SAHMI's taxa_counts.r also deduplicates (it takes unique() over barcode/umi/taxid), so its matrix is UMI counts too; what it does not do is carry that through to sckmer.r, whose k-mer statistics - and therefore the barcode-level denoising built on them - are computed over undeduplicated reads. Here the deduplication applies throughout, so the matrix and the statistics agree. Set false to count reads instead.

sc_host_de.description: Compare host expression between infected and bystander cells (SAHMI's host half)
sc_host_de.help_text: Wilcoxon rank-sum on log-normalised counts - Seurat's FindMarkers defaults, which is what SAHMI calls - between cells carrying a taxon and cells of the SAME TYPE that do not. Needs --sc_cell_metadata: which cell types carry a taxon is itself a result, so a pooled test recovers the difference between cell types and reports it as a response to infection.

sc_host_de_min_cells.description: Infected and bystander cells a group needs to be tested

sc_host_de_min_pct.description: A gene must be detected in this share of one side

sc_host_de_force_pooled.description: Run --sc_host_de without cell types, pooling every type
sc_host_de_force_pooled.help_text: Every row of the output is then stamped ALL_POOLED, because the result is not a within-type comparison and cannot be read as one.

sc_plate_based.description: Plate-based single cell (Smart-seq2): one library per cell
sc_plate_based.help_text: CSI-Microbes' second route. Every well is sequenced as its own library, so there is no barcode, no STARsolo and no --single_cell: each cell runs the ordinary bulk route and the cell-by-taxon matrix is those per-cell reports stacked. The samplesheet is then one cell per row, and --sc_cell_metadata must name the patient, plate or donor each cell came from as well as its type - without that every cell becomes its own stratum and the enrichment test collapses to the pooled one it exists to avoid.

sc_plate_min_reads.description: Reads of a taxon before a plate-based cell counts as carrying it
sc_plate_min_reads.help_text: Deliberately not --sc_min_umis: Smart-seq2 has no UMIs, and one amplified cDNA molecule can contribute hundreds of reads and a single UMI, so a read threshold and a UMI threshold are not interchangeable and the read one has to be stricter.

sc_ambient.description: Annotate each taxon with how strongly it is associated with cells rather than the ambient pool
sc_ambient.help_text: An ANNOTATION, not a filter. An empty droplet holds reagent contaminants, ambient soup, microbes released by lysed cells AND genuine extracellular organisms from the tissue - a luminal or mucosal organism is in that pool by construction, not by artefact - and no droplet-level comparison separates them. So a taxon as common in the medium as in cells is reported as `ambient_undecided`, never as contamination; only an external measurement of the kit settles that, which is what --decontam's blanks provide. What this does answer is whether a taxon is where the cells are, which is the strongest evidence droplet data can offer for an intracellular organism. Needs STARsolo's raw/ matrix as well as filtered/, so it is incompatible with --sc_cell_filter None.

sc_ambient_min_empty_umis.description: Host UMIs an empty droplet needs before it is used
sc_ambient_min_empty_umis.help_text: Excludes the sea of zero-count barcodes, which would otherwise inflate the empty-droplet denominator and make every taxon look cell-associated.

sc_ambient_max_empty_umis.description: ...and at most this many (0 = no upper bound)
sc_ambient_max_empty_umis.help_text: Set it to exclude near-cell barcodes just below the knee, which carry enough real content to behave like cells.

sc_ambient_min_droplets.description: Droplets a taxon must appear in to be tested

sc_ambient_enriched_ratio.description: Prevalence ratio at or above which a taxon is called cell-associated

sc_ambient_depleted_ratio.description: ...and at or below which it is called cell-depleted

sc_ambient_drop.description: Also write a drop list of the ambient and cell-depleted taxa
sc_ambient_drop.help_text: Off by default and only correct when the question is about INTRACELLULAR microbes. An extracellular organism genuinely present in the tissue is ambient by construction and would be on that list.

negative_controls.description: Negative-control libraries (blanks, empty wells, no-template controls) to judge every other library against.
negative_controls.help_text:
Four accepted forms: a comma-separated list of sample IDs; a file of one ID per line; `metadata.tsv:column` (rows whose column is true/yes/1/control/blank/negative); or `metadata.tsv:column:value` (rows whose column equals value exactly). The ID is the first column, as for `--da_metadata`.

This is the only filter in the pipeline whose verdict is per LIBRARY rather than per taxon, and the only one that can address index hopping or well-to-well carryover at all: those put genuine reads of a genuine organism into the wrong library, so no evidence filter can find fault with the reads, and the same taxon is then signal in one library and carryover in the next. A taxon is kept in a library only where it exceeds `--control_ratio` times its level in the controls, measured in counts per million classified reads; cells that fail are zeroed, and taxa that fail everywhere are removed outright. It costs recall - see docs/usage.md for the measured trade-off - and it is complementary to `--decontam`, not a replacement.

control_ratio.description: Multiple of the negative-control level a taxon must reach to be kept in a library.
control_ratio.help_text: Compared in counts per million classified reads, so it means the same thing in a shallow library and a deep one. It is not the only lever and on its own it is the wrong one: pushing it alone does reach full specificity on the CSI-Microbes plate, but by applying the same multiple to every taxon, and past about 50x it empties whole libraries of everything. Set `--control_min_reads` first and this second. 20 with a read floor of 30 is what turned that benchmark from 1 FAIL / 3 PASS into 0 FAIL / 4 PASS.

control_statistic.description: Which level to take from the controls: their mean, median or maximum.
control_statistic.help_text: `max` is the strict reading - clear the worst blank, not the average one - and reaches the same specificity at roughly a fifth of the `--control_ratio`. Prefer it when there are few controls, since one unusually clean blank cannot then set the threshold low.

control_min_reads.description: Reads a taxon needs in a library before the control ratio is consulted.
control_min_reads.help_text: Two jobs. A taxon absent from every control has a control level of the detection limit alone, which the ratio test would clear on very few reads; and carryover is small in absolute terms whatever the library depth - the four false positives on the CSI-Microbes plate carried 11 to 72 reads - so an absolute floor removes them at a fraction of the collateral damage a higher `--control_ratio` would cost.

control_floor_reads.description: The negative-control level never falls below what this many reads in a typical control library would be.
control_floor_reads.help_text: Absence from the blanks is a bound, not a measurement: it says a taxon is under one read in each of them, not that it is at zero. Without this floor the ratio test collapses to `any reads at all` for every taxon the controls happened to miss - on the CSI-Microbes plate that left specificity flat at 86.4% however high `--control_ratio` went, because the species leaking into the uninfected wells appeared in one blank out of twelve. Setting it to 0 restores that behaviour.

prevalence_filter.description: Drop any taxon present in at least this FRACTION of libraries (1.0 = every one). 0 disables.
prevalence_filter.help_text:
The fallback for cohorts with no controls, and a much cruder question: a reagent contaminant introduced at extraction is in every library, a biological signal usually is not. On the CSI-Microbes plate, dropping taxa present in all 180 libraries removed 87 taxa and 77.5% of all microbial reads without touching the spiked organism.

Only sound where a universally present taxon CANNOT be real. It is wrong for a mono-culture, wrong for a dominant gut commensal, and wrong for anything with an expected core microbiome. Off by default, and it reports what it removed.

prevalence_min_reads.description: Reads in a library for `--prevalence_filter` to count the taxon as present there.

export_biom.description: Also write the classification as a BIOM table.
export_biom.help_text: Purely for interoperability: nothing in this pipeline reads it. Built with kraken-biom from the same per-sample reports Krona uses (Bracken's redistributed report when Bracken ran, the Kraken2 report otherwise), then restricted to the taxa that survived the filters so it agrees with the combined tables. Written as BIOM 1.0 (JSON), which phyloseq's import_biom reads without rhdf5; pass `--fmt hdf5` through `ext.args2` for BIOM 2.1.

biom_metadata.description: Sample metadata to embed in the BIOM table. Defaults to --da_metadata.
biom_metadata.help_text: TSV with the sample id in the first column and one column per factor. Every sample classified in the run must appear, or the export stops and names the ones missing. Only read when --export_biom is set.

assembly.description: Assemble the non-host fraction de novo and score every taxon against the contigs.
assembly.help_text: The one line of evidence the other filters are blind to: they all count things about a taxon's reads, and a contig is a longer sequence. Reads placed by index hopping, or piled on a single conserved locus, do not assemble. Produces an evidence table only unless --contig_filter is also set.

assembly_assembler.help_text: MEGAHIT by default: the non-host fraction is overwhelmingly bacterial and archaeal, so there is no splicing for an RNA assembler to model, and what RNA-seq does impose is severe coverage skew -- which is what a multi-k metagenome assembler handles. metaSPAdes gives better contiguity for considerably more time and memory, accepts only paired-end reads, and has to concatenate a pool before it can assemble it.

assembly_pool.description: How libraries are pooled before assembly. Defaults to group when --da_grouping is set, otherwise all.
assembly_pool.help_text: Per-library assembly is close to useless on the cohorts this exists for: a false positive sitting at tens of reads per library assembles into nothing, and neither does a real taxon at that depth. Pooling by contrast group puts the libraries that should share an organism into one assembly.

assembly_min_contig_len.description: Shortest contig the assembler will report.

assembly_args.description: Extra arguments passed straight to the assembler.

contig_filter.description: Also remove taxa that had enough reads to assemble something and did not.
contig_filter.help_text: Off by default, and deliberately: a contig is strong positive evidence, but its absence is weak negative evidence because a genuinely rare organism does not assemble either. --contig_min_reads is the gate that keeps a taxon from being condemned for being rare. Contigs roll up the taxonomy, so a contig assigned to a species also supports the genus above it.

contig_min_reads.description: Below this many reads a taxon is recorded and not judged.

contig_min_length.description: A contig must reach this length to count as support.

contig_min_contigs.description: This many qualifying contigs are needed to support a taxon.

functional_profiling_options.title: Functional profiling options
functional_profiling_options.description: Optional HUMAnN 3 profiling of what the non-host community is doing.
functional_profiling_options.help_text: Off by default: HUMAnN needs large user-provided databases and is by far the most expensive step in the pipeline. It answers the question taxonomy cannot - which gene families and pathways are present - and its output is what the bundled exploreMetaTax app reads in its Gene families and Stratified tabs.

run_humann.description: Run HUMAnN 3 on the non-host reads.
run_humann.help_text: Requires --humann_nucleotide_db and --humann_protein_db, and cannot be combined with --skip_kraken2: HUMAnN selects pangenomes from a taxonomic profile, which is built with KrakenTools' kreport2mpa.py from Bracken's kreport (or Kraken2's under --skip_bracken) rather than by running MetaPhlAn as a second, disagreeing classifier. Note the consequence - HUMAnN keys on species (`s__`) lines, so clades left above species contribute nothing, which is also why Bracken's re-estimation is preferred as the source.

humann_nucleotide_db.description: ChocoPhlAn nucleotide database directory (use the species-named v201901_v31 release).
humann_nucleotide_db.help_text: HUMAnN builds its per-sample nucleotide database by matching each genus/species pair in the profile against ChocoPhlAn's filenames. Those are species-named up to v201901_v31 and SGB-named (t__SGB...) from vJan21 onwards. A profile derived from Kraken2/Bracken carries NCBI species names, which can only match the former - point this at an SGB release and the lookup selects nothing, leaving HUMAnN to run translated search alone.

humann_utility_db.description: HUMAnN utility mapping directory. Required for --humann_regroup.

humann_regroup.description: Regroup gene families onto another namespace, e.g. uniref90_ko for KEGG orthologs. Empty to skip.

humann_renorm.description: Renormalise abundances: cpm or relab. Empty to keep raw RPK.
humann_renorm.help_text: Raw HUMAnN output is in reads per kilobase, which is not comparable between libraries of different depth.

ai_annotation_options.title: AI annotation options
ai_annotation_options.description: Optional LLM-generated summaries in the HTML reports.
ai_annotation_options.help_text: Entirely opt-in: with `--llm_endpoint` unset the pipeline never contacts any LLM service. Any OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint works (a self-hosted vLLM/Ollama/llama.cpp server, or a commercial API). Everything sent is plain text taken from the pipeline's own QC tables - never a figure, never a read. Calls are strictly serialised so a single small server is never hit concurrently. The endpoint and the API key are scrubbed from every published report; the model name is kept as provenance.

llm_endpoint.description: OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions URL. Setting it enables the AI annotations.
llm_endpoint.help_text: Nothing AI-related happens unless this is set. The value is treated as a deployment secret: it is kept out of the parameter summary and scrubbed from the published reports. It is still visible in the Nextflow work directory (`.command.sh`), as any parameter is.

llm_model.description: Model name served at --llm_endpoint. Required whenever --llm_endpoint is set.
llm_model.help_text: Unlike the endpoint, the model name is deliberately kept in the reports: it is useful provenance for a summary a reader has to judge.

llm_api_key.description: Bearer token for the endpoint. Leave as 'dummy' for local servers that ignore it.

ai_insights.description: Which AI annotations to generate: 'all', 'no', or a comma-separated subset of multiqc,qualimap,taxonomy.
ai_insights.help_text: `taxonomy` narrates the combined Kraken2/Bracken tables and puts the result at the top of the MultiQC report. `multiqc` adds a summary under every section of that report. `qualimap` adds one to each per-sample Qualimap report. Has no effect unless --llm_endpoint is set.

llm_context_window.description: Model context window in tokens. Input tables are trimmed to fit it.

llm_timeout.description: Seconds to wait for one response before giving up on it.
llm_timeout.help_text: On timeout the box shows a 'timed out, please try again' placeholder rather than disappearing, so you can tell a failed summary from one that was never requested.

multiqc_ai_builtin.description: Also use MultiQC's own AI feature to write a global report summary.
multiqc_ai_builtin.help_text: Complementary to `--ai_insights multiqc`, which annotates individual sections. Note that MultiQC bakes the endpoint URL into the report it writes, so with this on the raw report is not published: the redacted copy in `multiqc_ai/` is.

multiqc_ai_summary.description: Length of MultiQC's builtin summary (--multiqc_ai_builtin only).

ai_qualimap_sections.description: Also summarise every individual Qualimap plot, not just the report as a whole.
ai_qualimap_sections.help_text: One extra LLM call per plot per sample, issued one at a time. For a real cohort that is hours of requests, which is why it is off by default.

diagnostics_options.title: Read accounting and diagnostics
diagnostics_options.description: Cross-tool read bookkeeping and library-chemistry checks.

skip_read_accounting.description: Skip the consolidated per-sample read-fate table.

host_carryover_taxid.description: Taxon counted as host leakage in the Kraken2 report (default: 9606, Homo sapiens).
host_carryover_taxid.help_text: Kraken2's standard databases contain the host genome deliberately, which makes it a free audit of the aligner: any non-host read that Kraken2 still calls host escaped depletion. A few percent is normal; tens of percent means the host reference is wrong or incomplete, and a second reference is worth adding.

run_polya_check.description: Check whether microbial reads in a poly(A) library came from capture or carry-over.
run_polya_check.help_text: Bacterial transcripts mostly lack poly(A) tails, so their presence in a poly(A)-selected library needs explaining. This counts internal poly-A/T runs in the non-host reads against a null built by shuffling each read (preserving its length and base composition): around 1 means carry-over, clearly above 1 means oligo-dT internal mispriming, which biases abundances towards A-rich transcripts. Only meaningful for poly(A)-selected libraries.

process_skipping_options.title: Process skipping options
process_skipping_options.description: Turn individual steps of the pipeline off.

skip_host_removal.description: Skip HISAT2 host depletion and classify the trimmed reads directly.

skip_kraken2.description: Skip taxonomic classification (and everything downstream of it).

skip_qualimap.description: Skip Qualimap BamQC on the host BAM.
skip_qualimap.help_text: samtools stats/flagstat/idxstats still run. Qualimap adds coverage depth and uniformity, duplication rate and mapping-quality distributions, which is what tells 'little host in this library' apart from 'wrong host reference'. It is the slowest step of the BAM QC, so it is worth skipping for very large BAMs.

execution_options.title: Execution options
execution_options.description: Caps and scheduler settings used by the `local` and `slurm` profiles.

resource_limit_cpus.description: Maximum CPUs a single task may request.
resource_limit_cpus.help_text: With `-profile local` this defaults to the number of cores on the machine; with `-profile slurm` to 128. Any task asking for more is capped instead of being rejected.

resource_limit_memory.description: Maximum memory a single task may request, e.g. `'128.GB'`.
resource_limit_memory.help_text: With `-profile local` this defaults to the machine's total RAM.

resource_limit_time.description: Maximum walltime a single task may request, e.g. `'24.h'`.

slurm_queue.description: SLURM partition to submit to (`-profile slurm`).

slurm_options.description: Extra options appended to every sbatch command, e.g. `'--account=myproject'`.

slurm_queue_size.description: Maximum number of jobs Nextflow keeps queued in SLURM at once.

compression_level.description: Compression level for every BGZF/gzip stream the pipeline writes. Unset leaves each tool at its own default.
compression_level.help_text:
Applied to `samtools sort -l`, `samtools view -l`, `samtools fastq -c`, `fastp -z` (clamped to 1, which fastp requires) and the `pigz`/`gzip` calls in the local modules. 9 buys roughly 5-10% on BAM for 2-3x the CPU, which is rarely the right trade on a large cohort; 1 is worth considering when the intermediates are deleted anyway.

Leaving it unset passes no flag at all, which is deliberately not the same as naming the number a tool already uses: a flag on the command line changes the task hash and un-resumes every cached task in the run. It also avoids quietly moving fastp, whose own default is 4 rather than the 6 samtools and zlib use. The vendored nf-core `HISAT2_ALIGN` writes its intermediate at its own default and is not covered - its output is re-encoded by the sort, which is.

alignment_output_format.description: Format for the sorted host alignments: BAM, or CRAM at roughly 40-60% of the size.
alignment_output_format.help_text: CRAM stores differences from the reference instead of the sequence, so it needs `--host` and the run stops without it. It is also refused alongside Qualimap (`qualimap bamqc` takes `-bam` and cannot open a CRAM) and alongside `--quantify_host` (featureCounts reads SAM/BAM only); both are checked at startup rather than allowed to fail per sample at the end of a run. samtools stats, flagstat and idxstats all read CRAM and still run. The reference is indexed once per pass rather than rebuilt inside every task. Targeted alignments stay BAM regardless.

cleanup_intermediates.description: Delete intermediates as soon as the pipeline knows nothing else reads them.
cleanup_intermediates.help_text:
Two things: the per-chunk HISAT2 BAMs, removed from inside the merge task once `samtools cat` has succeeded, and the downloaded FASTQs, removed once trimming and raw FastQC have both read them. Only files inside the work directory are ever removed, so a samplesheet's own FASTQs are skipped and reported rather than deleted; and the downloads are left alone under `--skip_trimming`, where they are still the working read set.
