Off by default because a deleted intermediate cannot be resumed: Nextflow will re-run the task that produced it, which for the downloads means fetching them again.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

differential_abundance_options.title: Differential abundance options
differential_abundance_options.description: Test which taxa differ between two groups of samples.
differential_abundance_options.help_text: Modelled on FGCZ's DiffShot apps (ezRun `EzAppDiffShot`). Runs on the combined Bracken count table, because both ALDEx2 and ANCOM-BC2 model integer counts: ALDEx2 draws Monte-Carlo instances from a Dirichlet posterior, ANCOM-BC2 estimates a per-sample sampling fraction from library size. MetaPhlAn relative abundances are rejected rather than rescaled.

da_metadata.description: TSV of sample metadata: sample id in column 1, factor columns after it. Setting it turns differential abundance on.
da_metadata.help_text: A separate file rather than a samplesheet column, because the --input_accessions and --input_dir routes have no samplesheet; one metadata file serves all three. Sample ids must match the ids in the Bracken table (with --group_runs_by experiment those are SRX/ERX accessions, not SRR/ERR).

da_method.description: Method(s) to run: 'ancombc', 'aldex2', or both comma-separated.
da_method.help_text: Each method has its own container - no biocontainer carries both - so naming both runs two processes over the same table. ANCOM-BC2 corrects for compositional bias and handles structural zeros; ALDEx2 works in centred log-ratio space with Monte-Carlo sampling. Disagreement between them is informative.

da_grouping.description: Metadata column holding the categorical variable to test on.

da_sample_group.description: Value of --da_grouping treated as the test group. Coefficients read sample-over-reference.

da_ref_group.description: Value of --da_grouping used as the reference level.

da_covariates.description: Additional metadata columns to adjust for, comma-separated.
da_covariates.help_text: Extends the model formula (ANCOM-BC2 fix_formula; ALDEx2 switches from the t-test path to aldex.glm). Leave unset for the unadjusted model.

da_prevalence_min.description: Keep taxa seen (>1 read) in at least this fraction of samples.

da_relabund_min.description: Keep taxa holding at least this percentage of the pooled reads.

da_lib_cut.description: ANCOM-BC2 minimum library size; smaller samples are dropped by the method.

da_p_threshold.description: Adjusted p-value below which a taxon counts as significant.

da_lfc_threshold.description: Absolute log2 fold change a taxon must also reach to count as significant.

target_taxid.description: Extract this taxon's reads from the classification and follow them to differential expression of its own genes.
target_taxid.help_text:
Turns a Bracken row into an experiment. Kraken2's per-read output records which read it assigned where, so the reads for a taxon can be pulled back out with KrakenTools, aligned to that organism's own genome, counted against its annotation and tested between the same two groups as everything else. Comma-separated for several taxids.

Requires --kraken2_save_readclassifications (the per-read record) and --target_reference (the genome). --target_gtf adds gene counts and, with --da_metadata, the differential expression.

Reads reach this branch because a k-mer classifier assigned them, and a classifier's false positives look exactly like true positives. The alignment rate in `targeted/log/` is the check: reads that really came from the target align to its genome, mis-assigned reads do not.

target_reference.description: Genome for --target_taxid: NCBI accession, taxid, FASTA, or prebuilt HISAT2 index.
target_reference.help_text: Detected from the value exactly as --host is: `GCF_*`/`GCA_*` is an assembly accession, digits alone are a taxonomy ID, a directory (or `.tar.gz`) is a prebuilt index, anything else on disk is a FASTA.

target_gtf.description: Annotation for --target_reference. Without it the branch aligns and stops at the BAM.

target_include_children.description: Also take reads Kraken2 assigned below the target taxon.
target_include_children.help_text: On by default: a read placed at a strain below the target species is evidence for that species.

target_include_parents.description: Also take reads Kraken2 could only place above the target taxon.
target_include_parents.help_text: Off by default, and it warns when enabled. A read Kraken2 could only place at the genus is consistent with the target species but is not evidence for it, and this option quantifies it as though it were.

target_max_reads.description: Cap on extracted reads per sample.
target_max_reads.help_text: KrakenTools applies this cap whether or not you set it; it is exposed so that hitting it is a decision rather than a silent truncation.

target_de_method.description: Gene-level DE method(s) for the targeted taxon: deseq2, edger, or both.

host_transcripts.description: Host transcriptome FASTA. Quantify host expression with kallisto instead of featureCounts.
host_transcripts.help_text:
Pseudoaligns the TRIMMED reads against the transcriptome, so it is independent of host depletion and of --quantify_host. The resulting matrix goes through the same differential expression as the featureCounts route.

kallisto is offered for quantification only, never for host depletion: a transcriptome index can only remove reads that came from an annotated transcript, so intronic, intergenic, repeat and satellite reads would survive depletion and be classified as spurious microbes - which is precisely what the second host assembly exists to prevent.

host_tx2gene.description: Two-column TSV (transcript id, gene id) to sum kallisto transcript abundances to genes.
host_tx2gene.help_text: Without it the matrix stays at transcript level. Summing to genes is also what makes rounding kallisto's fractional est_counts for DESeq2 a small approximation rather than a real one, because the apportioning that rounding damages is mostly within a gene.

target_transcripts.description: Transcriptome FASTA for --target_taxid. Quantify the extracted reads with kallisto instead of aligning them.
target_transcripts.help_text: Replaces the whole align-and-count route for the targeted taxon: no genome, no index and no GTF are needed. The trade-off is that the alignment rate - the check that Kraken2's assignment was real - is no longer produced; kallisto's run_info.json p_pseudoaligned is the nearest equivalent.

target_tx2gene.description: Two-column TSV (transcript id, gene id) for --target_transcripts.

kallisto_args.description: Extra arguments passed to kallisto quant.

kallisto_fragment_length.description: Estimated fragment length, single-end input only.
kallisto_fragment_length.help_text: kallisto measures the fragment-length distribution from paired reads and cannot infer it from one end, so single-end quantification needs an estimate and the abundances inherit whatever error it carries.

kallisto_fragment_sd.description: Standard deviation of the fragment length, single-end input only.

host_de_method.description: Gene-level DE method(s) for the host counts: deseq2, edger, or both comma-separated.
host_de_method.help_text: Runs when --quantify_host and the --da_* contrast are both given, on the gene x sample matrix merged from featureCounts. Deliberately not ALDEx2/ANCOM-BC2: those model compositional data, where only proportions are meaningful, whereas gene counts have a scale that DESeq2's median-of-ratios and edgeR's TMM estimate directly. The contrast, covariates and thresholds are taken from the same --da_* parameters the microbial side uses, so one metadata file describes both halves of the library. Set to null to skip.

host_de_min_count.description: A host gene needs this many reads in at least --host_de_min_samples samples to be tested.
host_de_min_count.help_text: Applied before the test, not after: filtering the results afterwards would leave the adjusted p-values computed against a gene set that was never really tested.

host_microbe_correlation.description: Correlate host gene expression against microbial abundance across samples.
host_microbe_correlation.help_text:
Monteleone et al.'s third layer, and the analysis --quantify_host exists for: both sides come from the same library, so an association between them is not confounded by sample handling the way two separate assays would be. Spearman on log-CPM host expression against relative microbial abundance, BH-adjusted.

Opt-in because it is easy to run and impossible to interpret on a small cohort. With n samples the smallest attainable Spearman p-value is 2/n!, so with five samples nothing beyond three gene-taxon pairs could ever clear BH at 0.05 - and a grid of thousands returns an empty table that reads like a negative result. The step computes that arithmetic up front and refuses rather than producing one.

host_microbe_top_genes.description: Test only the N most variable host genes (0 = all).
host_microbe_top_genes.help_text: Every gene added multiplies the number of tests by the number of taxa, and multiple-testing correction is what limits this analysis long before compute does.

host_microbe_top_taxa.description: Test only the N most abundant taxa (0 = all).

da_samples_to_drop.description: Sample ids to exclude entirely before any analysis, comma-separated.
